title: License footprint buckets, SLA-aligned support tiers, and QSA readiness for Private/VPC
creator: Riya Kapoor
description: Goal: Define a compact, sales-friendly packaging framework for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that ties license fees to predictable operational units ("footprint buckets"), maps support tiers to SLA commitments, and produces a pre-baked QSA/enterprise-security questionnaire bundle the sales team can ship with initial proposals. This ticket covers pricing experiments, contract language templates, upgrade cadence options, and the security artifacts checklist required for RFPs and vendor risk assessments.
acceptance_criteria: Three license footprint bucket proposals (Small/Medium/Large) documented with pricing anchors, example customer profiles, and unit economics (expected ARR per bucket)
Support tier matrix that maps to response/restore SLAs, escalation paths, and optional managed-upgrade windows; drafted contract clauses for each tier
A/B experiment plan for testing per-node vs. per-GPU vs. per-cluster pricing in pilot customers, with clear success metrics (conversion, deal size, time-to-close)

QSA-ready security artifact bundle: SOC2/Security summary, network topology template, KMS/HSM integration notes, audit-log examples, patching/upgrade policy, and answers to top 30 vendor questionnaire items
Legal sign-off on base contract language for license fee, termination, upgrade cadence, and indemnity; Security sign-off on the QSA bundle
Enablement kit for Sales + Solutions Engineering including pricing calculator, objection-handling doc, and contract playbook
notes: Motivation: Sales teams are losing time customizing price comps and security bundles for every enterprise RFQ. A narrow set of opinionated packages should speed pricing conversations and reduce legal churn.
Key trade-offs: simpler bucketed pricing improves sales velocity but may leave money on the table for very large customers. We will include optional overage/scale credits to protect revenue upside.

Upgrade cadence options: (A) Managed quarterly minor upgrades + optional guaranteed major upgrade windows, (B) Customer-controlled upgrades with Redwood-provided hotfix channel, (C) Continuous opt-in upgrades for dev/test buckets. Need legal input on liability for forced upgrades.

Entitlement metric candidate list: concurrent inference capacity (vGPU-equivalents), daily token throughput, licensed node count, or commit-based reserved throughput. Initial preference from Infra & Solutions Eng is vGPU-equivalents for predictability of unit economics.

We should prepare two contract templates: 'Standard Enterprise Private' (recommended) and 'Strict Air-Gap' (for heavily regulated customers) with differing support granularity and upgrade obligations.
